_comment: Every sentence the site says about the query API and the agent tools. The tools under webmcp serve both the pages and the MCP server at /mcp. The build writes them into openapi.json, the agents page, llms.txt, each dataset page and its Markdown twin, site.js and functions/_tools.json. {name} is filled from limits; `code` becomes code in HTML. The gate checks limits, operators, metrics and parameters against functions/_query.js and functions/_api.js.

site.summary: Australian government open data republished as CSV, Excel, JSON, Parquet, SQLite, DuckDB, GeoJSON and GeoPackage at URLs that never change. Every release is a dated, immutable version with schema, provenance and a diff. Run by National Digital. No government agency has endorsed it.
site.file_formats: parquet, csv, csv.gz, ndjson and duckdb are on every table version. xlsx is there up to {xlsx_mb} MB of CSV and {excel_rows} rows, json up to {json_mb} MB of NDJSON, and sqlite up to {sqlite_mb} MB of CSV. gpkg, and geo.parquet for points, exist only for datasets that declare geometry, with geojson up to a {geojson_mb} MB file, and pmtiles only for polygon and line layers. A version's manifest.json lists each format the limits left out, with the reason, under formats_left_out, and that set never changes. A version whose manifest has no caps field was fetched before these limits: it also has arrow, its xlsx stops at the Excel row limit, and its json and geojson stop at {json_rows} rows.

api.summary: The query API returns only the rows you ask for, as JSON, NDJSON or CSV, from the same typed rows as the files. It needs no key.
api.rows: `/api/v1/datasets/<slug>/rows` filters, selects, orders and pages any dataset.
api.aggregate: `/api/v1/datasets/<slug>/aggregate` counts, sums, averages, minimums and maximums by group.
api.versions: Without a version the API answers from the newest loaded version, and that answer changes when the publisher releases again. Put `versions/<date>/` before `rows` or `aggregate` for an answer that never changes. `/api/v1/datasets/<slug>/versions` lists the loaded versions.
api.filters: Each filter is `field=operator.value` in the query string, and every filter must match. A number or date field compares as a number or date, and a text field compares as text. Values are case-sensitive, except that `like` and `ilike` ignore case in the ASCII letters A to Z. Prefix `not.` to negate a filter, as `not.eq.value`.
api.provenance: Every JSON answer carries the version, licence and attribution. CSV and NDJSON answers carry them in response headers.
api.terms_limits: The query API allows {requests} requests in {window_seconds} seconds from one address. The MCP server counts each row tool call as two requests, against its own limit of {requests} requests in {window_seconds} seconds from one address. Files have no rate limit.
api.rate_limit: The API allows {requests} requests in {window_seconds} seconds from one address. Above that it answers 429 for {block_seconds} seconds with a `Retry-After` header, a `RateLimit-Policy` header and a JSON body that gives the limit. Every API answer carries the same `RateLimit-Policy`. A client should wait the `Retry-After` seconds, or read the files, which have no limit.

neq.label: is not
neq.description: Not equal to the value. A blank cell does not match.

gte.label: at least
gte.description: Greater than or equal to the value.

lte.label: at most
lte.description: Less than or equal to the value.

like.label: matches
like.description: Matches a pattern where `*` stands for any run of characters, ignoring case in the ASCII letters A to Z.

ilike.label: contains
ilike.description: The same as `like`. Both ignore case in ASCII letters only, so É and é differ.

in.label: is one of
in.description: Equal to any value in the list. A value cannot contain a comma.

is.null.label: is blank
is.null.description: Blank in the source, or suppressed by the publisher.

select.description: Fields to return, comma-separated. Every field when absent.

order.description: `field.asc` or `field.desc`, comma-separated. The publisher's row order when absent.

limit.description: Rows per page, 1 to {limit_max}. {limit_default} when absent.

offset.description: Rows to skip. The `next` URL in each answer sets it for you.

format.description: `json`, `ndjson` or `csv`. JSON carries the provenance header, and the others carry it in response headers.

slug.description: The dataset's slug, as in its page URL `/d/<slug>/`.

version.description: A dated version loaded for queries, from the versions path. Answers for a dated version never change.

rows.description: Rows of {title} in {when}, filtered and paged.

aggregate.summary: Counts, sums, averages, minimums and maximums by group
aggregate.description: Groups and totals of any dataset in {when}. Filters work as they do on rows.

versions.summary: The versions loaded for queries, newest first, with the URLs to query each

responses.200: Rows with the version, licence and attribution. `next` is the URL of the following page, or null.
responses.200_versions: Loaded versions with row counts and URLs.
responses.400: The query names a field the dataset does not have, or a value of the wrong type.
responses.404: The dataset or version is not loaded for queries.
responses.429: More than {requests} requests in {window_seconds} seconds from one address. Blocked for {block_seconds} seconds. Wait `Retry-After` seconds.

webmcp.intro: Pages register WebMCP tools through `navigator.modelContext` when the browser exposes it. The row tools call the query API, so their filters, counts and sums cover the whole table and an agent can answer a question about the data without leaving the page. On a dataset page they default to that dataset and describe each of its fields with the publisher's own wording and the values it holds. The search form and the backlog form carry declarative WebMCP annotations as well. Without any of it, the URLs above do the same work.
webmcp.page_note: On this page slug defaults to {slug} ({title}), and where lists its fields.

search_datasets.title: Search datasets
search_datasets.description:
Find the slug of a served dataset. Start here for any question about Australian government data, since the other tools read only the datasets this finds.
Every word in query must match the title, summary, publisher, keywords or a field name. A word matches its plural and other endings but never as a prefix, so bus does not find business.
Up to 50 matches come back in one answer, with no paging. If nothing matches, try fewer or broader words, then search_catalogue.
Each call costs one of the {requests} queries each address may make in {window_seconds} seconds.

query.description: Words from a title, publisher or field name

slug.description: The id every other tool takes

latest.description: URL of the newest version's whole file

results.description: Matches, best first when the search index is loaded

get_dataset.title: Read a dataset
get_dataset.description:
Read a served dataset's data package and full version history: licence, attribution, whole-table files and the version dates diff_versions and the version parameter take. It carries no rows. To answer from the rows use query_rows or count_rows, and for field names use list_fields.
slug is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, the part after /d/ in a dataset page URL, such as au-road-deaths.
The whole history comes back in one answer, with no paging. It needs no key or sign-in, and costs nothing against the rate limit. A slug that is not served returns a 404 error.

datapackage.description: The Frictionless data package: description, licence, attribution string, source, and resources with the URL, format and size of the whole file in each format

versions.description: Every version with its date, the date its data is as at, row count, source hash and fetch time

list_fields.title: List a dataset's fields
list_fields.description:
List a served dataset's fields, with their types, descriptions, ranges and values, before querying it. Call it before query_rows or count_rows unless you already know the exact names and values, because where matches values exactly and an unknown field is an error. It also names the key fields diff_versions compares on and the partition fields list_partitions accepts.
slug is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, the part after /d/ in a dataset page URL, such as au-road-deaths.
The answer describes the newest version, in one page. The call costs nothing against the rate limit. A slug that is not served or not loaded for queries returns an error.

attribution.description: The publisher's attribution string, to show with any answer

fields.description: Each field's name, type and publisher's description, with min and max for numbers and dates and values when it holds few

key.description: Fields that identify a row, compared on by diff_versions. Empty when none is declared

list_partitions.title: List partition files
list_partitions.description: List the download files that split a served dataset's newest version by one field, such as one file per year. Use it to hand someone a slice of the data as a file. It gives file links and no rows, so to answer a question use query_rows or count_rows instead, and for the whole table as one file use get_dataset. field must be one of the partition_by fields that list_fields names, and any other field returns a 404 error. Every value comes back in one answer, with no paging. The call costs nothing against the rate limit.

field.description: A partition field named in the data package, for example crash_year or loc_local_government_area

version_base.description: The version these files belong to

partitions.description: One entry per value: the value, its row count and the URL of a JSON file with every row holding it

query_rows.title: Query rows
query_rows.description:
Read individual rows of a served dataset, filtered across the whole table. For totals and breakdowns use count_rows, and for files use get_dataset or list_partitions.
Field names and values for where, select and order come from list_fields.
Filters hold at most 90 values per call, and a list value cannot contain a comma.
version must be one of the two newest versions.
One page holds up to limit rows, and offset steps through the rest until next_offset is null. An unknown field or version returns an error naming it.
Each call costs two of the {requests} queries each address may make in {window_seconds} seconds.

select.description: Fields to return. Every field when absent.

limit.description: Rows to return, 1 to 500. 50 when absent.

offset.description: Rows to skip. next_offset in each answer gives the next page.

rows.description: The rows, with the fields in select or every field

matched.description: Rows in the whole table that match where

next_offset.description: offset for the next page, or null on the last

query.description: The query API URL for the same query, which answers while the API has the version loaded

file.description: The Parquet file the answer was read from, when it came from the file

manifest.description: The version's manifest, with its licence, source, hash and fetch time, when the answer came from the file

attribution.description: The publisher's attribution string, to show with any answer

count_rows.title: Count and sum rows
count_rows.description:
Count, sum, average, minimum or maximum rows of a served dataset across the whole table, grouped by up to three fields. For the rows themselves use query_rows.
Field names and values for group_by and where come from list_fields.
sum and avg need a numeric or true-or-false field. min and max take any field.
version must be one of the two newest versions.
Groups come back largest first, and truncated means raise limit or narrow where. An unknown field or version returns an error naming it.
Each call costs two of the {requests} queries each address may make in {window_seconds} seconds.

group_by.description: Fields to group by, for example ["crash_severity"]. One total when absent.

metric.description: `count`, or `sum`, `avg`, `min` or `max` of a field written as `sum.field_name`. `count` when absent.

limit.description: Groups to return, 1 to 1000. 100 when absent.

groups.description: One object per group, holding the group_by fields and the metric value, largest first

truncated.description: True when more groups exist than limit

matched.description: Rows in the whole table that match where

query.description: The query API URL for the same query, which answers while the API has the version loaded

file.description: The Parquet file the answer was read from, when it came from the file

manifest.description: The version's manifest, with its licence, source, hash and fetch time, when the answer came from the file

attribution.description: The publisher's attribution string, to show with any answer

diff_versions.title: Compare versions
diff_versions.description: Compare two consecutive versions of a served dataset row by row on its key fields, to see what a publisher changed between releases. from and to must be adjacent dates in the version history from get_dataset, older first. Any other pair returns a 404 error, so step through a longer span one pair at a time. A dataset with no key, which list_fields shows as an empty key, gets row counts only, and a dataset with one version has nothing to compare. One answer holds the counts of rows added, removed, changed and unchanged, the keys of the rows added, removed and changed, and up to ten changed rows with their old and new values. The call costs nothing against the rate limit.

key.description: Key fields compared on. Empty when none is declared

schema.description: Fields added, removed and retyped between the versions

note.description: Present when no key is declared and only row counts are compared

truncated.description: True when a key list stops at its cap

examples.description: Up to ten changed rows, each with its key and the fields that changed from and to

search_catalogue.title: Search government portals
search_catalogue.description:
Search every dataset listed on Australia's government portals, including the many publicdata.au does not serve yet. Its records describe data held elsewhere, which cannot be queried here.
Use it when search_datasets finds nothing, to find where a dataset is published, or to pick one for upvote_dataset.
query matches every word against the title, summary and publisher, as search_datasets does.
A page holds 20 records, those that can take a vote first. Pass next_offset as offset for the next page, up to 5000.
Each call costs three of the {requests} queries each address may make in {window_seconds} seconds.

query.description: Words from a title, description or publisher

votable_only.description: Leave out records that cannot take a vote

offset.description: Rows to skip. next_offset in each answer gives the next page.

catalogue_read.description: Date the portal lists were read

next_offset.description: offset for the next page, or null on the last

url.description: The record on the publisher's portal

state.description: votable or chosen takes a vote, served is already readable, closed cannot be built

reason.description: Why a closed record cannot be built

list_backlog.title: List the build backlog
list_backlog.description:
List the datasets people have asked publicdata.au to build, most votes first. Use it to see what is wanted or under way, or to check that a vote counted.
To add a vote use upvote_dataset. To read a dataset that is already served use search_datasets.
Votes on catalogue records that no entry has claimed yet come back apart, under the vote key search_catalogue uses.
The whole backlog comes back in one answer, with no paging, and the call costs nothing against the rate limit.

entries.description: Register entries that are not live yet, most votes first

status.description: backlog and assessing wait for votes, building is under way, blocked cannot be built yet

source.description: The publisher's own page for the data

blocked_reason.description: Why a blocked entry cannot be built yet

catalogue_votes.description: Votes on catalogue records no register entry has claimed yet, most first

vote.description: The record's vote key, which search_catalogue finds

upvote_dataset.title: Vote for a dataset
upvote_dataset.description:
Add one anonymous vote for a government dataset that publicdata.au does not serve yet, so it is built sooner. To read a served dataset use search_datasets, and to see the votes so far use list_backlog.
slug is a vote key from search_catalogue, such as act-3u5a-ve4j, or a list_backlog slug.
A dataset that is served, being built or closed returns an error saying it is not open for votes.
No identity is recorded, so a vote cannot be withdrawn, and a second vote from the same caller on the same day adds nothing. The answer gives the dataset's vote total after this call. The call costs nothing against the rate limit.

slug.description: The vote key of a search_catalogue row, or a slug from /backlog.json

votes.description: The dataset's vote total after this call

webmcp.where: Filters by field name, applied to the whole table. A value may be a scalar for an exact, case-sensitive match, a list of scalars to match any of them, null to match blank or suppressed cells, {"min": n, "max": n} for an inclusive range, or {"like": "*text*"} for a pattern where * is the wildcard and case is ignored in ASCII letters. A blank cell never matches a scalar, a list or a range.
webmcp.version: A version date, YYYY-MM-DD, from get_dataset. The newest version loaded for queries when absent.

mcp.title: publicdata.au
mcp.registry_description: Search, filter, count and sum Australian government open data, with every version kept.

connect.note: On the web and in the desktop app.

mcp.intro: `https://publicdata.au/mcp` is a remote MCP server over Streamable HTTP with the same tools, defined in the same place, so a tool added to the pages is added here too. It needs no key and no account. Its row tools also answer for the versions the query API does not load, from each version's Parquet file once that file is rebuilt under the query profile. A query that would read too much of a file is refused with DuckDB SQL that answers it from the file. The row tools are held to the query API's limit of {requests} queries in {window_seconds} seconds from one address, and each call is two queries because it also counts the matching rows. Add it to Claude Code with `claude mcp add --transport http publicdata https://publicdata.au/mcp`, add the URL in Claude as a custom connector, or give it to any client that connects to remote MCP servers. Each dataset with a table is also a resource at `https://publicdata.au/d/<slug>/fields.json`, which lists its fields with their types, the publisher's descriptions, their ranges and the values they hold, so an agent can read a dataset's shape before it writes a query.
mcp.resource: The fields of {title}, from {publisher}: each field's type and the publisher's description, the range of numbers and dates, and the values a field holds when it has few. Use them to write where filters for query_rows and count_rows.
mcp.resource_template: The fields of one dataset by slug: types, the publisher's descriptions, ranges and the values each field holds. Find slugs with search_datasets or resources/list.

What Australian government data is there on road crashes, and who publishes it?

mcp.prompts_note: It also offers the prompts {prompts}, and suggests dataset slugs as a client types one.

ask_dataset.title: Ask a dataset
ask_dataset.description: Answer a question from one dataset, with its fields attached and the answer cited to the version it came from.

question.description: What to find out from the data

ask_dataset.text: Answer from the publicdata.au dataset {slug}. Its fields are attached. Use count_rows for totals and breakdowns and query_rows for individual rows, and filter with where using the field names and values listed. Say which version the answer came from and give the attribution string and the query URL.
ask_dataset.question: Question: {question}

find_data.title: Find data on a topic
find_data.description: Search publicdata.au for datasets on a topic and say what each holds.
find_data.text: Find datasets on publicdata.au about {topic} with search_datasets. For each match, read its fields with list_fields, then say in a sentence what it holds, who publishes it, its licence and the years it covers.

tool_text.version must be one of the two newest ve: version can be any date in the version history from get_dataset.

parameters.version: A version date, YYYY-MM-DD, from get_dataset. A version the query API does not load is read from its Parquet file. The newest version when absent.
parameters.order: field.asc or field.desc, comma-separated. When absent, and for ties, a version the query API loads keeps the publisher's order, and any other version the order of its Parquet file, which follows the dataset's declared sort where it has one.

mcp.privacy: The MCP server records nothing about who calls it or what they ask. To keep the rate limit, it counts row tool calls per address in Cloudflare's cache for {window_seconds} seconds.
mcp.instructions: Australian government open data, republished at URLs that never change. Find a dataset with search_datasets, read its fields with list_fields, then answer from the whole table with query_rows or count_rows. A dataset that is not served yet can be found with search_catalogue and voted for with upvote_dataset. Every answer names the version it came from and the publisher's attribution string. When you show the data to a person, use the attribution string, say it came from publicdata.au and link to the version the answer came from, https://publicdata.au/d/<slug>/v/<version>/. Use of this server is under https://publicdata.au/terms/.
